hook: SCP-2998 opens with an apology from the records office: the file is infected, and you will have to click through several false versions before reaching the real one. Take that at face value and keep going, because each iteration is a different kind of story wearing the same item number. It is long, so set aside a proper sitting.
whyItMatters: Its unusually wide tag list, from science fiction and cosmic horror to crime and military fiction, is not decoration; each false iteration really does switch genre. It is one of the most ambitious uses of the revision-chain format, pushing it past simple escalation into alternate timelines, a collapsed civilization, and finally an unreadable page. The appearance of Maria Jones and Researcher Rosen as recurring names gives the chain a human thread to hold onto.
thingsToNotice:
The early iterations play as first contact by eavesdropping: two test subjects try to explain a vast alien grudge with gangland comparisons, and the clumsy translation sells the scale. Later versions answer the question of what happens when that grudge spills over, first in a bleak invasion file, then in a document rewritten by a fanatical successor to the Foundation.

The footnote conversation hidden inside the garbled version is the emotional peak, two survivors finding each other on a broken network and reaching for a famous anomaly as a last resort. Then the redacted page, the folksy epigraph, and the dull final version invite you to wonder whether that ending actually worked. The opening notice is the key: the true file is the boring one, and the article quietly suggests why.

related.note: It turns up near the end, and knowing its nature adds weight to the plan.
Another chain of file versions charting a contamination that reaches the Foundation itself.
